leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part B002 prize naming Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, with B001 and B035 as the stated alternatives (B035 and B001 in the order given by El-Manira and Sandberg; B001 then B035 for the other four). The citation wordings differ slightly but all cover the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form as the basis of incretin therapy. Sandberg opened with Knudsen in place of Mojsov and has moved to the shared trio, but describes this as a judgement under the three-person cap and not a finding that Knudsen's contribution is minor. Members do not share a view on how firmly Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is established, nor on whether excluding Knudsen is a neutral choice; several say it is a choice with a cost.

areas_of_agreement: All six explicitly prefer a single-part prize for B002 with the same three laureates (Drucker, Holst, Mojsov); no member lists a second prize part in the round-1 configuration.

Members describe the GLP-1 work as a complete arc from gut-hormone physiology and the truncated active peptide, through receptor biology, to therapies with large, independently confirmed outcome-trial benefit in type 2 diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease.
Every member names attribution as the strongest reservation, specifically the contested credit for identifying the active peptide and the absence of Habener from the credited names.
Members agree that B001 (optogenetics) and B035 (CAR-T) are the only named alternatives, and that each has its own attribution problem that makes it no cleaner than B002.
Several members ask for the primary record on the Mojsov, Habener and Holst priority question to be checked before the discovery trio is treated as fixed.
scientific_disputes: Whether Knudsen's long-acting analogue design (half-life extension that made liraglutide and semaglutide usable) counts as scientific invention that belongs in a discovery citation, or as industrial development that can be left out. Perlmann and Svenningsson lean toward discovery framing; Linnarsson, El-Manira and Sandberg stress that excluding her is a defensible judgement, not an obvious one.

For B001, whether the prize should recognise the channel discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and the neuronal deployment (Boyden, Deisseroth) on equal footing, and how a tool or method should be weighed against a therapy. Svenningsson's opening trio was Boyden, Nagel and Deisseroth; other members' trios were Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel, and several members criticised both for omitting a credible claimant.

For B035, whether Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T-cell work is the same achievement as CAR design by June and Sadelain, given that Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept is not among the credited names.

Whether the pathway-level cases raised in responses (B051 cGAS-STING, B021 unfolded protein response, B017 TNF blockade) are better judged as earlier or less mature than the leading candidates or on a different originality standard; these were discussed by a few members and are not in any member's preferred configuration.
attribution_disputes: B002: priority for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide among Mojsov, the Habener group and Holst is described as contested by several members, none of whom could verify it from primary records. Habener is outside the credited list.

B002: the third laureate slot is the live decision, between Mojsov (discovery side) and Knudsen (long-acting analogues). Five members hold Mojsov; Sandberg's opening preference for Knudsen was withdrawn under the cap, and Linnarsson and Svenningsson say they would reconsider if the Mojsov evidence proved weak.
B001: six credited names and a three-person cap leave Bamberg, Hegemann, Miesenböck or Boyden out of any trio, and members disagree on which omission is most defensible.
B035: Eshhar is not credited, and members differ on whether Rosenberg should be paired with the CAR designers.
maturity_disputes: B002 is treated as mature by all six (about two decades of replication, outcome trials), with only long-term safety and durability of weight loss noted by some as still being characterised; no member argues this undercuts the core discovery.

B001 is described as mature and exceptionally influential in experimental neuroscience, but El-Manira, Svenningsson and Wahren-Herlenius point to a clinical payoff that is still early and ask how much weight demonstrated benefit to patients should carry for a Medicine prize.
B035 is described as mature by El-Manira (approved products, long follow-up), with attribution, not maturity, as the main concern.
B051 and B021 were called promising but earlier on disease-level or therapeutic evidence by Linnarsson and Wahren-Herlenius; these views are in responses and not in preferred configurations.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Perlmann discloses co-authorship with Svenningsson and once with El-Manira, and El-Manira discloses a 2009 paper with Perlmann; none involves a credited name on any shortlisted ballot and no member requests recusal.
Linnarsson and Sandberg disclose co-authorship with each other; neither is a credited name and no recusal is requested.
Perlmann notes work with Ronald Evans, and Wahren-Herlenius lists Kuchroo and Sonesson as co-authors; none is credited on a shortlisted ballot.

Svenningsson and El-Manira note that their neuroscience background touches B001 by topic only and that they have tried to discount this; no member reports a documented involvement with B002, B001 or B035.
questions_for_round2: Can the secretariat check the primary record on who identified and characterised the active truncated GLP-1 peptide (Mojsov, the Habener group, Holst), so that the committee can decide whether the evidence supports naming Mojsov and how Habener's claim should be treated?
If the Mojsov evidence is judged weak or unresolvable, should Knudsen take the third slot, and if so, will the citation say plainly that the framing has moved from discovery to translation?

If Mojsov stays, what citation wording credits the physiology and the active form without implicitly writing out Habener and Knudsen, and will the record state explicitly that excluding Knudsen is a judgement under the cap?
Is the committee prepared to recommend B002 as a single part, or does any member wish to propose a second distinct part (B001, B035 or another candidate) with named laureates and a citation?
If B002 stalls on credit, which fallback does the committee prefer, B001 or B035, and on what weighting of a method versus a therapy?

For any fallback, can the committee name three people without a serious attribution injustice: for B001 a split among Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg, Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenböck, and for B035 a treatment of Eshhar and of Rosenberg's role?
summary.chair_observation: The six round-1 files are identical in structure: a single B002 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, with B001 and B035 as alternatives. The open matters are not whether B002 leads but who holds the third name, how the citation is worded, and whether the fallbacks are viable. These depend largely on attribution evidence that no member says they have verified.
